name: Ashes in the Signal
subcategory: pirate radio / the Gray Zone political commentary
creator: Collective broadcast, primary voice: 'Baba Ferric' (identity unknown)
description: An irregular pirate audio broadcast originating from somewhere in the Gray Zone's Ward 9 district, transmitted over hijacked infrastructure frequencies and later mirrored to gray-market neural feed channels. The anonymous host known only as Baba Ferric delivers slow, deliberate political commentary in a voice that mixes Yoruba proverb structures with Rust Belt English and occasional Polish phrases, dissecting corponation policy, the Gray Zone resource allocation failures, and the quiet violence of debt enforcement. Episodes are never scheduled — they simply appear.
medium: pirate radio broadcast / gray-market neural feed mirror
cultural_impact: Baba Ferric's phrase 'the rent on your own breath' — used to describe mandatory BCI subscription fees for basic civic access — became one of the most repeated political slogans in the Gray Zone throughout the 2200s.
controversy: Three individuals have been arrested by Axiom Municipal Authority on suspicion of being Baba Ferric; none were charged and none confirmed the identity. Corponation media has characterized the show as 'destabilization content' and pressured neural feed aggregators to block mirrors.
story_hooks: A journalist trying to identify Baba Ferric discovers that the voice is a composite — assembled from at least four different people's speech patterns using black-market audio synthesis.
An episode of Ashes in the Signal contains information about a corporate data breach that hasn't happened yet — someone is feeding the show intelligence from inside a Tier 4 corponation.

Baba Ferric goes silent for forty days; when the signal returns, something in the cadence and phrasing is subtly different, and longtime listeners are divided about whether the show has been compromised or replaced.
